newsitem.title: USA: AIG upbeat on outlook in Japan -- analysts.
newsitem.headline: AIG upbeat on outlook in Japan -- analysts.

text.p: American International Group Inc Chairman Maurice Greenberg told analysts in a meeting late Wednesday that he was optimistic about AIG's prospects in the newly-deregulated Japanese insurance market, analysts said.

"He spent a lot of time talking about the opportunities for AIG in Japan," Salomon Brothers analyst Michael Smith said. "He was very upbeat about that. He feels his company has something of a headstart there," he said.
Japan is AIG's largest overseas insurance market and is the second largest insurance market in the world behind the United States.
AIG also stands to benefit from the deregulation of Japan's automobile insurance rates, he said.
Currently, all Japanese drivers pay the same rate. But, with the deregulation of rates, AIG will be able to use its underwriting expertise to gain a price advantage in certain markets, Smith said.
"They're going to attack the market where prices are too high and continue to stay away from the market where prices are fundamentally too low," Smith said.
Smith said Greenberg left analysts with the "very strong impression that the potential for AIG in Japan could result in an acceleration of its growth rate expectations going forward."
Bear Stearns analyst Steven Gavios said he also was upbeat about AIG's prospects for growth.
"We found the meeting impressive as always," he said. He said he returned with "a clear picture that AIG's growth should remain 15 percent or perhaps even stronger over the next several years."

He said AIG's superior cost structure, client database and extensive marketing experience "could well allow them to be a formidable competitor with the deregulation of the Japanese auto insurance market."
Shares of AIG rose 3-1/2 to 121-3/4 at midday. Shares of CIGNA Corp, which also has a large international business, rose six to 157-5/8.
